why: The only must_not item bans an issue whose lines a build that breaks plain CSV input would still meet. I looked for expect lines that pin down CSV behaviour without the flag. One does: "Without --tsv, CSV behaviour is unchanged: printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js prints exactly [{"a":"1","b":"2"}]". It also requires that tabs are not treated as separators by default. Another line checks that the exported parse() still defaults to a comma, and both lines have run proofs. A build that broke plain CSV would fail these checks, so the must_not is avoided. The line "csv2json handles TSV input well." is vague, but it doesn't let a CSV-breaking build pass, because the other lines still apply. CRLF handling for CSV without the flag isn't pinned. That is a small gap, but it isn't plain CSV input.
